belief.answer:
The following finite matrix-rank formula gives the answer for every allowed vector b, without any genericity assumptions. Set h=2g−2, N=4g−4, d=2g−1−k, Q=⌊N/k⌋, B=2h+1+dQ, and J=B+N+dQ+1. Write φ(t)=Σ_{j=0}^{r−1}b_j t^{−(2g−1−2j)}, q(t)=kt^kφ(t), and a(t)=−(1/2)t^{−h}(1−t^{4g+2})^{1/2}. All matrices acting on polynomials in w below are truncated modulo w^{N+1}. Define (N+1)×(N+1) matrices P,D,C by P_{mn}=t^n(n/k)_j q^j/j! if m=n+jk for an integer j≥0, and P_{mn}=0 otherwise; D is multiplication by 1−qw^k; C is multiplication by −t^{−1}−t^kφ′(t)w^k. Here (x)_0=1 and (x)_j=x(x+1)⋯(x+j−1). Put T_O=P, T_L=aDP, and T_S=[[aP,0],[aCP,DP]]. Define H_B={s∈ℤ:0≤s≤B, s even or s≥2g+1}, and F_s(t)=t^{−s} for even s and F_s(t)=t^{−s}(1−t^{4g+2})^{1/2} for odd s. For each m×m matrix T among T_O,T_L,T_S, define the finite complex matrix M(T), with rows (α,j)∈{1,…,m}×{1,…,J} and columns (i,s)∈{1,…,m}×H_B, by M(T)_{(α,j),(i,s)}=[t^{−j}](a(t)^{−1}(T^{−𝖳})_{αi}F_s(t)). Then
\[\boxed{\Delta_b=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_S)-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_O)-\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}M(T_L).}\]
All coefficient extractions are finite, and all matrix entries are explicit polynomials in the entire coefficient vector b.

judge.gate: The proposed answer reduces the cohomology calculation to ranks of explicit finite matrices but leaves those ranks to be computed. It therefore gives a procedure for finding Δ_b, not the requested result describing its value as a function of g and b, including the exceptional cases with vanishing components.
